dishes.name: Griot
dishes.description: Griot is a dish in Haitian cuisine. It consists of pork shoulder marinated in citrus, which is braised and then fried. It is commonly served at parties.

dishes.name: Diri ak djon djon
dishes.description: Diri djondjon (black mushroom rice) is a native dish of Haiti. It is essentially a meal consisting of rice made with edible black mushrooms called djondjon. The meal is more common in the northern region of the country and therefore can be considered a regional specialty.

dishes.name: Soup joumou
dishes.description: Soup Joumou (; French: soupe au giraumon, lit. ‘pumpkin soup’) is a soup native to Haitian cuisine. In 2021, soup joumou was added to the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List.

dishes.name: Pikliz
dishes.description: Pikliz is a pickled condiment in Haitian cuisine. It can be eaten fresh or fermented for taste and health benefit. Pikliz (pronounced PEE-kleez) can be understood based on the word pickle and the French word piquer (meaning to sting).

dishes.name: Fritay
dishes.description: Fritay, (; Haitian Creole: Fritay; French: Friture Haïtienne) collectively known as Fritaille, are street foods and culinary styles associated with Haitian culture.

dishes.name: Akasan
dishes.description: Akasan (sometimes AK 100) is a popular Haitian beverage made from corn kernels, anise stars, vanilla and cinnamon. It is drunk either warm or cold, often as a breakfast beverage. Akasan is known for its rich sweetness and thickness.
